data.narrative:
Xaira Therapeutics is a seed-stage biotech company founded by Marc Tessier-Lavigne that has raised $1.0B to date. The valuation analysis draws on a competitive set of 3 public peers (RXRX, TEM, ONT.L) and 8 private companies in the Biotech & Health sector, including Colossal Biosciences, Abridge, and Recursion Pharmaceuticals.

Of the three valuation methods examined, only Stage-Progression anchoring proved applicable. This method applies a 2.5x step-up multiplier typical of Seed-to-next-stage advancement against the $1.0B total capital raised as a baseline valuation proxy, yielding $2.5B. Peer-Median triangulation was not viable due to insufficient narrow-stage comparables in the dataset (fewer than 3 same-stage or adjacent-stage peers met filters). Public-Comp Anchoring could not be applied because Xaira's revenue—required to apply the public sector P/S median of 5.5x—is not on file, which is standard for pre-revenue or early-clinical private biotech.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $2.1B to $2.9B, centered on $2.5B. Given the single-method triangulation and lack of disclosed financial performance or clinical milestones in the data, significant uncertainty persists around the appropriate stage advancement multiple and fair-value positioning relative to disclosed peers. Revenue disclosure or clinical-stage specification would materially strengthen conviction in this range.
